title: Securities Trading Policy (including Inside Information)

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Chairman of a Dexus entity board; distinguished in the Business Approval Table, requiring approval from an Independent Director and General Counsel.

tiers.name: Independent Director
tiers.description: Independent Directors of Dexus entities; approval required from the Chairman (or another Independent Director if the Chairman is absent) and General Counsel.

tiers.name: Chief Executive Officer
tiers.description: The CEO; approval required from the Chairman (or an Independent Director if absent) and General Counsel.

tiers.name: Executive General Manager
tiers.description: Executive General Managers, including Key Management Personnel; approval required from the CEO and the Head of Governance.

tiers.name: Employee
tiers.description: The defined term 'Employee/s' collectively covers Directors of Dexus entities, all Employees (including Key Management Personnel), Contractors and temporary employees, and their Associates. Substantive prohibitions (Inside Information, short-term gain, margin lending, hedging of unvested securities, trading windows) apply to this tier without differentiation; approval for ordinary Employees is sought from the relevant EGM and the Head of Governance.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into a transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities

windows.start_anchor: the day after half yearly and yearly results are announced to the market

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The CEO, in consultation with the Chair, may identify additional trading windows or cancel any trading window at any time (effective immediately on notification to all Employees), and, in exceptional circumstances, may impose a restriction on trading in DXS, ADI/DXI or DXC by Listed Securities Funds. Cancellation of a window is notified to all Employees (not confidential), but a refusal of an individual clearance to trade, or its withdrawal, must be kept confidential by the affected Employee.

rules.detail: A derivative or other arrangement entered for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of unvested securities is banned; the prohibition is purpose-based (hedging) rather than a general ban on derivatives dealing.
rules.evidence: entering into a transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities

rules.detail: No provision expressly addresses derivatives dealing over vested securities; the hedging ban is limited to unvested securities, and the Policy does not define 'securities' or 'financial product' to expressly include third-party-issued derivatives referencing Dexus securities, so it is unclear whether the general trading-window/approval regime (which addresses 'trading in Dexus securities' and 'financial products managed by Dexus') extends to a bank-issued OTC derivative.
Absolute ban on hedging arrangements over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: entering into a transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is expressly limited to unvested securities; hedging of vested securities is not separately addressed.
No mention of prepaid forwards, monetisation or similar structures.
Short selling is not named or otherwise addressed (distinct from the separate short-term-gain trading ban).
Securities lending is not named or otherwise addressed.
CFDs are not named and are not clearly caught by any defined term in the Policy.
Outright ban on trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities, with no vesting distinction and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities

rules.detail: The ban on margin lending activities necessarily prohibits granting security over Dexus securities to a margin lender; no broader provision addresses granting a charge, lien or pledge outside a margin lending structure.
rules.evidence: trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities

rules.detail: Only 'margin lending activities' are named; the Policy does not use a broader phrase such as 'or any other secured financing arrangement', so a bilateral loan from a bank secured by a pledge of the shares, not structured through a margin lending facility, arguably sits outside the literal wording, though it would still need Media Test and section 10 approval as a dealing in Dexus securities.
rules.evidence: trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities

rules.detail: Ban on trading in Dexus securities for short term gain, defined as a purchase and sale within 30 days.
rules.evidence: trading in Dexus securities for short term gain (defined as a purchase and sale within 30 days)

clearance.approver: An Independent Director; and General Counsel
clearance.post_trade_to: Compliance team (contract note or transaction advice)
clearance.evidence: All trades by Employees in listed and unlisted financial products managed by Dexus require prior approval in accordance with the Business Approval Table. Chairman: An Independent Director; and General Counsel.

clearance.approver: Chairman (during absence, another Independent Director); and General Counsel
clearance.post_trade_to: Compliance team (contract note or transaction advice)
clearance.evidence: Independent Director: Chairman (during absence, another Independent Director); and General Counsel

clearance.approver: Chairman (during absence an Independent Director); and General Counsel
clearance.post_trade_to: Compliance team (contract note or transaction advice)
clearance.evidence: Chief Executive Officer: Chairman (during absence an Independent Director); and General Counsel

clearance.post_trade_to: Compliance team (contract note or transaction advice)
clearance.evidence: Executive General Manager (including KMP): CEO; and Head of Governance

clearance.approver: Relevant EGM (during absence, another EGM); and Head of Governance
clearance.post_trade_to: Compliance team (contract note or transaction advice)
clearance.evidence: There may be circumstances when this approval is not granted. Reasons for this may be withheld. Where approval is withheld, the Employee is to keep that fact confidential and not disclose it to anyone. ... Where approval is granted, the trade must be executed within 5 business days. If the trade is not executed within this timeframe, approval will need to be re-sought. A clearance to trade may be withdrawn if circumstances change.

short_term.evidence: trading in Dexus securities for short term gain (defined as a purchase and sale within 30 days)

exceptions.evidence: participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by Dexus (subject to insider trading provisions in the Corporation Act).
acquisition of Dexus securities through a distribution reinvestment plan
acquisition of Dexus securities through a security purchase plan available to all retail securityholders
acquisition of Dexus securities through a rights issue
the disposal of Dexus securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Dexus securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Employee is a beneficiary)

exceptions.approver: CEO and/or Company Secretary (via the Head of Governance)
exceptions.evidence: Trading in financial products outside the trading windows may be granted in situations of severe financial hardship provided the Employee is not in possession of Inside Information. ... approval sought from the CEO and/or Company Secretary prior to placing the order to sell.

exemption_authority: Trading outside the trading windows may be approved by the CEO and/or Company Secretary (request referred via the Head of Governance) only for severe financial hardship, where the Employee is not in possession of Inside Information and provides sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available; if granted, the trade must be executed within 5 business days. Approval for ordinary in-window trades or other dealings may otherwise be withheld under the Business Approval Table, including where a dealing would fail the 'Media Test', with reasons able to be withheld and refusals kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as the Director or Employee taking advantage of his or her position in an inappropriate way? ... Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Media Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a structure that clears every express rule can still be refused approval on this subjective reputational standard, so a funded collar with a bank remains subject to discretionary compliance sign-off regardless of technical permissibility.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (the Policy addresses hedging of un-vested securities and 'trading in Dexus securities'/'financial products managed by Dexus' requiring approval, but does not define Securities or financial product to expressly extend to third-party-issued derivatives referencing Dexus securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike comparable policies, DXC's policy has no explicit definition sweeping in bank-issued OTC puts/calls over vested securities, creating some ambiguity as to whether the collar's derivative legs are directly regulated at all, separate from the underlying share dealing and insider trading rules that plainly still apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is worded narrowly around 'margin lending activities'; a bespoke bilateral loan from a bank secured by a share pledge, not routed through a margin lending facility, arguably falls outside the literal wording, though it would still need approval under the general 'trading in Dexus securities' clearance regime and would likely fail the Media Test in substance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where approval is granted, the trade must be executed within 5 business days. If the trade is not executed within this timeframe, approval will need to be re-sought.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring, documenting and executing a collar (and its secured loan) within a 5-business-day approval window is tight; any delay requires re-applying for approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: reference to Dexus Securities includes reference to Dexus (ASX:DXS), Dexus Industria REIT (ASX:ADI1) and Dexus Retail Convenience REIT (ASX:DXC).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single policy governs dealings across the whole Dexus stapled group, so a DXC-specific collar for a director or executive is assessed under the same group-wide rules, approvers and trading windows as DXS and DXI.

summary: A funded collar is not clearly prohibited on the face of this policy, but nor is it clearly permitted, because the policy's derivatives and financing language is narrower and less precise than in comparable policies. Section 7 bans hedging arrangements and margin lending activities only for unvested securities and margin-lending-structured financing respectively, and does not contain a general OTC-derivatives or broad secured-financing catch-all, so a collar over vested securities and a bilateral bank loan secured by a share pledge (not a margin lending facility) arguably sit outside the literal wording of the express prohibitions. However, any dealing in Dexus securities still requires prior approval under the Business Approval Table (approver depending on the Employee's role, e.g. CEO/General Counsel for the Chairman, relevant EGM/Head of Governance for an ordinary Employee), must occur within a trading window (or under the severe-financial-hardship exemption), must not occur while holding Inside Information, and critically must satisfy the subjective 'Media Test' under which approval will be refused if the dealing could be perceived as taking advantage of position. In practice, compliance is likely to treat a funded collar and its secured loan as economically equivalent to hedging and margin lending and refuse approval, but the policy does not state this outcome expressly, leaving room for negotiation with General Counsel/Head of Governance case by case.
